name: Minimum Reborn
description: A rendering-focused rebuild of Minimum with a native in-game control panel. Engine or Optimized renderer mode, zero-pixel and off-screen draw fast-outs, particle pool caps, an editor-only culling policy, and a No Additional Input Delay ordering mode that moves all mod bookkeeping behind the game's update. Physics, input handling and the game's FPS cap are never changed. Windows build for Geometry Dash 2.2081.

profile.name: Profile
profile.description: Balanced is the default: optimized renderer, particle culling, scene culling off because GD batches level objects, editor culling on. Default keeps the engine renderer and full particle effects. Performance and Extreme lower the particle cap and enable gameplay scene culling. Editing a profile-owned setting switches to Custom. Nothing here changes physics, input handling or the game's FPS cap.

enabled.name: Enable Minimum Reborn
enabled.description: Master switch. Off restores the game's normal draw path immediately, without a restart.

target-fps.name: Target FPS
target-fps.description: The frame rate you want to hold, usually your monitor's refresh rate. Used only to color the overlay and to pick the frame-time thresholds. It does not change the game's FPS cap.

renderer-mode.name: Renderer Mode
renderer-mode.description: Engine: every draw call goes through the unmodified game renderer; the mod only measures. Optimized: the mod's draw hooks run - zero-pixel sprites, empty batch nodes and eligible off-screen particles are not submitted. Draw order, blending, glow, clipping, shaders and transforms are never changed. This is not a replacement rendering backend.

sprite-fast-path.name: Sprite Draw Fast-Out
sprite-fast-path.description: Skips the draw call for sprites that cannot produce any pixel: opacity 0, zero scale on an axis, or an empty content size. Children are still drawn normally, so the image is unchanged. On by default.

skip-idle-particles.name: Skip Idle Particle Draws
skip-idle-particles.description: Does not issue a draw for particle systems that have no live particles. Looks exactly the same and is free to keep on.

cull-offscreen-particles.name: Skip Off-Screen Particles
cull-offscreen-particles.description: Does not draw relative-position particle systems whose worst-case reach does not touch the screen. They keep updating, so emission timing and motion are unchanged when they scroll back. Free and grouped systems are always drawn.

particle-cull-mode.name: Particle Culling Mode
particle-cull-mode.description: Conservative keeps 128 world units of margin around the screen, so a system is only skipped when it cannot come into view before the next frame. Aggressive keeps 8 units and skips more: use it to see how much draw work culling removes, not on a level where you care about the edges. Draw-only either way; simulation is never skipped.

scene-cull.name: Scene Object Culling
scene-cull.description: Gameplay-only scene culling for unbatched sprites. Skips a draw when the sprite's whole quad is outside the viewport plus a margin (160 conservative, 16 aggressive). Off by default because GD batches level objects. The Level Editor has its own separate policy under Editor Culling.

cap-particles.name: Cap Particle Pool Size
cap-particles.description: Limits how many particles one system can hold. The pool, quad and index buffers are allocated for the capped size, so nothing can index out of bounds. Only affects systems created after the change: re-enter the level.

particle-cap.name: Particle Cap
particle-cap.description: Maximum particles per system. 256 is close to normal, 128 trims extreme particle spam, 32 is aggressive. Thin effects are the only visual cost.

spawn-budget.name: Particle Spawn Budget
spawn-budget.description: How many particle systems per frame get a full pool during a level. 0 is off. Systems past the budget still exist but get a pool of 4, so a burst of effects looks thinner instead of stalling the frame.

adaptive-cap.name: Adaptive Particle Cap
adaptive-cap.description: Experimental and off by default. While drawn frames stay slower than the Target FPS, the particle pool is lowered in steps (never below 24) and logged; it relaxes back to the configured cap when frames recover. Only affects systems created afterwards, so the effect appears as new effects spawn. It never changes timing, physics or input.

no-input-delay.name: No Additional Input Delay
no-input-delay.description: Moves every piece of Minimum Reborn bookkeeping out of the pre-update part of the frame: the scheduler counter runs after the game's update, and statistics, benchmark sampling and the Win32 focus probe run after the scene is drawn. The mod then executes no instrumentation before the game processes input and simulation. Ordering change only: it does not modify game input code, physics or the FPS cap, and no hardware latency measurement is claimed.

low-latency.name: Low Latency (drain GPU queue)
low-latency.description: Calls glFinish() once the frame has been submitted, so the driver cannot keep several frames queued ahead of the display and a click is not stuck behind them. Off by default. Honest trade-off: with vsync on, the buffer swap already blocks, so this mostly adds a driver flush and wait - the gain is clearest when the game is not vsync-bound, and it can cost average frame rate, especially on hybrid or Optimus laptops. It does not touch physics, timing or the game's FPS cap. Windows only: the drain is compiled into the Windows draw path.

editor-culling.name: Editor Culling
editor-culling.description: Draw-only visibility and particle culling while the editor is open. Object data, selection, dragging, undo, copy/paste, triggers and saving are never touched. GD batches level objects, so only unbatched editor sprites and particle systems can actually be skipped; the panel shows the real counters.

editor-cull-mode.name: Editor Culling Mode
editor-cull-mode.description: Conservative keeps 160 world units around the viewport; Aggressive keeps 16. Both are draw-only. The editor has its own policy and does not inherit the gameplay scene-cull setting.

render-gate.name: Render Gate (experimental)
render-gate.description: Experimental and OFF by default. Draws at Render FPS while the scheduler keeps the game's normal rate, so physics, collision and input processing still run every tick. Only useful above the display refresh rate (uncapped FPS). It delays what you see by up to one render interval, so leave it off if you want the most direct visual feedback. Do not use it together with mat.draw-divide.

render-gate-fps.name: Render FPS
render-gate-fps.description: Draw rate while the Render Gate is on. Set it to your monitor refresh rate.

background-throttle.name: Throttle Drawing In Background
background-throttle.description: While the game window is not focused, draw at Background FPS. Logic and audio keep running normally. Turn off if you record the game with window capture while it is unfocused.

background-fps.name: Background FPS
background-fps.description: Draw rate while the game window is not focused.

timer-resolution.name: 1 ms Timer Resolution
timer-resolution.description: Asks Windows for 1 ms timer wakeups instead of about 15.6 ms, which reduces uneven frame pacing when the game waits for the next frame. Slightly higher idle power use. Undone when switched off.

disable-power-throttling.name: Disable Power Throttling
disable-power-throttling.description: Opts the game process out of Windows efficiency mode (EcoQoS) so it is not moved to slow cores or low clocks. Useful on laptops and Windows 11.

process-priority.name: Process Priority
process-priority.description: Above Normal is safe. High can starve OBS or Discord. Applied immediately, no restart needed.

show-overlay.name: Performance Overlay
show-overlay.description: Shows FPS, average and p95 frame time, 1% low, logic updates per second, CPU time inside the draw call and the skip counters. Updated four times a second; it creates no nodes per frame.

benchmark-seconds.name: Benchmark Duration
benchmark-seconds.description: Length of the benchmark started from the pause menu. Recording starts on the first unpaused frame after you resume; pause screens are not counted. The result reports average, p50/p95 frame time, 1% low, draw CPU time, culling deltas and batch draws, and is written to the Geode log too.

overlay-detail.name: Overlay Detail
overlay-detail.description: Compact shows FPS, average frame time and 1% low. Detailed adds frame-time p95, logic rate, draw CPU time, the bottleneck hint and the skipped-draw counters. 'draw ms' is CPU time inside the draw hook, not GPU time.

overlay-corner.name: Overlay Corner
overlay-corner.description: Where the overlay is drawn. Top Right is the default because the level HUD uses the top-left corner for the attempt counter.

overlay-opacity.name: Overlay Opacity
overlay-opacity.description: Opacity of the overlay text, 20 to 255.
